fullTextParagraphs: A little planning can lead to a lot more success. Gather your project team for a kickoff to align on the project's purpose and how you’ll work together to achieve it.
Determine project team members and their roles.
Define the project vision, mission, and mission tests.
Get your team aligned on the purpose of the project and how you’ll work together to achieve it.
Video conferencing with screen sharing or meeting space.
Digital collaboration tool (see templates).
Optional: physical whiteboard, markers, timer, and sticky notes.
Bring your team together at the beginning of a project to agree on what success looks like and start creating a plan to achieve it.
About this Play
Instructions

A project kickoff meeting is the first meeting with the project team and the project client (when applicable). This meeting establishes the project’s purpose, roles, responsibilities, and success markers.

Starting a project without a kickoff meeting is like starting a road trip without a map or directions. You’ll probably waste a lot of time, money, and energy getting to your destination – if you make it at all. Running the Project Kickoff Play sets the course for smooth collaboration and success.
The project kickoff typically takes place after the statement of work or project poster has been finalized and everyone is ready to get started.
The kickoff meeting is an opportunity to align your team around the project's “who, what, where, when, why, and how.”
Research shows there are proven benefits to gaining consensus around several of the topics discussed during a project kickoff:
Clarifying roles Clearly understanding roles and responsibilities can drive better outcomes by improving communication, coordination, trust, and team member satisfaction.
Set the stage by building psychological safety Teams with established norms that encourage collaboration and open dialogue perform better.
Vision When employees understand the vision (or why their work matters and how it affects others), their job performance, persistence, and productivity increase.
Clear success criteria, or mission tests Unclear requirements lead to costly rework. Outlining what success looks like and fixing things early often reduces confusion and costs later.
Before running this Play, identify your project sponsor, project leader, facilitator, core team, and stakeholders. (One team member might hold multiple roles.)
Project sponsor (or executive sponsor): The most senior stakeholder who has the most to gain or lose from your project’s delivery
Project leader: Sets the vision on what the team is delivering and why
Facilitator: Responsible for keeping the kickoff meeting flowing and focused
Core team: The people who do the project work
Stakeholders: Anyone with insights, information, feedback, or a vested interest in the project’s outcome
The Project Kickoff Play is flexible and can easily be adapted. Use the other Plays under “Variations” below as inspiration to customize the agenda for your team.
Not everyone needs to attend all parts of the kickoff. Keep any variations you add to just the core team.

Bring together the project sponsor, leader, and facilitator to draft a project vision, mission, and mission tests in a collaborative document, such as a Confluence page, whiteboard, or Trello board. The rest of the project team will participate in a 5-minute silent pre-read of the project poster. Next, the team will revise these elements during the kickoff meeting:
Vision: Your “why,” or the impact your team will make when the project is completed. Why are you pursuing this project?
Mission: Your “what” and “how.” What are you trying to do? How will you achieve your vision?
Mission tests: Your “when.” What will it look like when this project is successful? These tests indicate if your mission is on track and create a shared definition of “done.”

Ask your project sponsor to open the session by welcoming attendees and sharing a quick overview of the project and its relationship to the organization. If your sponsor isn’t available to join the session, you can ask them to record a quick video, like a Loom, ahead of time to share with the group.
At the beginning of the project kickoff meeting, share an overview of the agenda, along with some mutual agreements to keep the conversation productive:
Collaboration: Let’s work together to setup this project for success.
Good enough: Let’s aim for progress, not perfection. Gather enough information to create a shared understanding, then continue refining it in the future.
Possibility: Let’s suspend judgment about what has been, and keep an open mind about what could be.

Start with a short icebreaker to get everyone focused and in the right mindset. If the group doesn’t already know each other, have each person introduce themselves, explain their role in the project, and answer one icebreaker question. (See the Icebreakers Play for inspiration.) If the group is already familiar, skip straight to the icebreaker.

This is the most important aspect of the project kickoff: rallying the team around a shared purpose that can inspire and guide them. Begin by sharing the initial vision, mission, and mission tests created before the kickoff. Then, break attendees into three groups: one for vision, one for mission, and one for mission tests. Give each group 20 minutes to refine the initial statements. Next, bring the group back together to present and discuss their revised statements. Make any agreed-upon changes, then vote to formally accept them for the project. You can (and should) refine these elements later in the project as you uncover new information.
Try a Roman vote to get a quick gauge on consensus and/or concerns:

Invite your project leader to close the meeting by thanking the group for their collaboration, providing any feedback or closing thoughts, and recapping the next steps. On your list of action items, assign a team member to update the project poster with your agreed-upon vision, mission, and mission tests.
All work and no play make a dull project team. Arrange a fun event shortly after the kickoff, like virtual games or a social outing.
If there’s time during your kickoff meeting, or in a separate session, you can use other Plays to continue outlining the project plans.
Set Objectives and Key Results.
Make a DACI Decision-making Framework to determine who will drive the project and who will be accountable, consulted, and informed.
Map out your project’s proposed timeline, tasks, and milestones so you can Prioritize, as a Team.
Create a workback plan or a backlog of tasks using a tool like Trello, a Jira project management template, or a Confluence project plan template.
As the project moves along, revisit these plans and your project post to document progress and make any needed adjustments.
For a shorter meeting, try limiting the template to questions about working hours, ideal environment, communication preferences, and learning styles before discussing anything longer and deeper.
Following the icebreaker, run a short Retrospective Play to discuss what you’ve learned from past projects and how you will apply those lessons to this project.
Use the Working Agreements Play to create a set of mutual agreements about how the team will work together to get the job done efficiently and effectively.

After you agree on your project’s purpose, what are the individual roles on the project? Run the Roles & Responsibilities Play to provide team members with clarity on how they will each contribute towards the project’s success. This Play also helps identify any gaps in skills or functions so you can address them early on in the project.
Start a conversation with other Atlassian Team Playbook users, get support, or provide feedback.
Map out and optimize cross-team relationships at the beginning of a project.
Clarify individual responsibilities and find gaps that need to be filled.
Create shared norms that help your team work well together to achieve common goals.
Uncover the root of a problem and explore possible solutions.
Get the latest Plays and work life advice when you sign up for our newsletter.

notes.explain: 指团队成员对项目的核心目标和意义形成共识，确保所有人朝着同一方向努力
notes.example: Before starting the marketing campaign, we need to align on the primary purpose of increasing brand awareness.

notes.phrase: project vision, mission, and mission tests
notes.meaning: 项目愿景、使命和使命检验标准
notes.explain: vision指项目的长远理想状态，mission指项目的核心任务，mission tests则是衡量是否完成使命的具体标准
notes.example: Our project vision is to become the market leader, our mission is to innovate sustainable solutions, and mission tests include reducing carbon footprint by 30%.

notes.explain: 明确团队成员的具体职责和衡量项目成功的标准，确保责任清晰、目标可衡量
notes.example: The project charter clearly outlines each team member's roles, responsibilities, and success markers for the quarterly objectives.

notes.phrase: sets the course for smooth collaboration
notes.explain: 比喻项目启动会如同设定航向，确保团队协作顺畅无阻，朝着共同目标前进
notes.example: A well-conducted kickoff meeting sets the course for smooth collaboration throughout the entire product development lifecycle.

scenario.title: Agreeing on the goal before assigning work
english: A project team is preparing a product launch, but people have different ideas about what success means.
The team has not agreed on the main goal, how to measure it, or what is outside the project scope.
You suggest settling those points before assigning tasks.
chinese: 项目组正在准备产品发布，但成员对“成功”各有理解。
团队还没有明确主要目标、衡量方式，以及哪些事项不属于本项目范围。
你建议先把这几项说清楚，再分配任务。

firstAttempt.prompt: 项目启动会上，大家对“项目成功”理解不同。请用英文建议先明确目标、成功标准和项目范围，再讨论分工。
firstAttempt.sample: Before we assign the work, could we agree on the project goal, how we’ll measure success, and what is in scope? That will give the team a shared basis for planning.
firstAttempt.rationale: 启动会先对齐目标、范围和成功标准，团队才有共同依据安排工作。

words.example: The project kickoff meeting is scheduled for next Monday to align all stakeholders.
words.translation: 项目启动会定于下周一举行，以协调所有利益相关者。
words.note: kickoff常用于项目、活动或计划的开始阶段，表示正式启动

words.example: Before assigning tasks, let’s align on what a successful launch means.
words.translation: 分配任务前，我们先对怎样才算发布成功达成一致。
words.note: align on强调在目标、方向或理解上达成共识，常用于团队合作场景

words.example: The team used mission tests to check whether each option supported the project goal.
words.translation: 团队用目标检验来判断每个方案是否支持项目目标。
words.note: 这是特定项目语境中的说法；日常项目沟通中，success criteria 更常见。

words.example: We need clear success markers before assigning the work.
words.translation: 分配工作前，我们需要明确衡量成功的指标。
words.note: success markers 指判断项目成果的指标；项目沟通中也常说 success criteria。

words.example: We’ll use video conferencing for the kickoff so remote teammates can join.
words.translation: 我们会用视频会议开启动会，让远程同事也能参加。
words.note: video conferencing指通过视频技术进行的远程会议

words.example: After the kickoff, we’ll keep the scope and decisions in the shared project space.
words.translation: 启动会后，我们会把范围和决定记录在共享项目空间里。
words.note: digital collaboration指利用数字技术和工具进行的团队协作

structure.original: Gather your project team for a kickoff to align on the project's purpose and how you’ll work together to achieve it.
analysis: 主句结构为祈使句'Gather your project team for a kickoff'，其中'Gather'是动词，'your project team'是宾语，'for a kickoff'是目的状语
不定式'to align on the project's purpose and how you'll work together to achieve it'作目的状语，其中包含两个并列的宾语：'the project's purpose'和'how you'll work together to achieve it'
第二个宾语'how you'll work together to achieve it'是一个由how引导的名词性从句，其中包含不定式'to achieve it'作目的状语
structure.transfer: Before assigning tasks, agree on the project goal, how success will be measured, and what is outside the scope.

rewrite.bad: Let’s divide the tasks now. We can decide what success means after the project starts.
rewrite.good: Before we assign the work, could we agree on the project goal, how we’ll measure success, and what is in scope? That will give the team a shared basis for planning.
rewrite.translation: 分配工作前，我们能否先对齐项目目标、成功标准和范围？这样团队就有共同的计划依据。
rewrite.pattern: Before we [assign the work], could we agree on [the goal, success measure, and scope]?

cloze.prompt: Could we agree on what the portal should help customers ___?
cloze.why: 先定义用户要完成的任务，再讨论项目方案。

cloze.prompt: Could we agree on how we’ll measure ___?
cloze.why: 共同确定成功标准，避免各自理解不同。

cloze.prompt: Define what is in scope before assigning the ___.
cloze.why: 先对齐范围，再拆分项目工作。

dictation.text: Sarah, the marketing manager, and Tom, the sales representative, are preparing for a new product launch campaign.
Sarah wants to focus on brand awareness while Tom prioritizes immediate lead generation.

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否先明确这个门户要帮助客户完成什么？

translationPractice.prompt: 我们能否约定怎样衡量成功？
translationPractice.answer: Could we agree on how we’ll measure success?

translationPractice.prompt: 分配任务前，我们也先明确本期范围。
translationPractice.answer: Let’s also define what is in scope before we assign the work.

options: You're wrong. We need to focus on leads now, not brand awareness. That's what sales cares about.
